tree.approach: Does a statistic on cylindric tableaux carry Warnaar's Eq_generalise, and is it a transfer-matrix twist?

children.approach: Lemma 1: edot_{n-r} = (x_1..x_n)^{-1} f_r, hence (x..)^k * Eq_generalise at t=1 = det_k(F_{-i+j,N} - F_{i+j,N}) = HKKO Thm 3.3 RHS. The y-sum enters row i by multilinearity exactly because the t-weight is absent; for t != 1 it depends on the COLUMN index j and cannot.

Control: three wrong weight functions in place of c^-_{2h,w} (c^+, unsigned, wall at w-1) all FAIL HKKO eq (3.6) at (h,w,n)=(1,2,4),(1,4,5),(2,2,4) while the true c^- passes. The t=1 comparison is not a constant function of the claim.

Control on my reading of Eq_generalise, including the exponent t^{(k+l+1)y^2 - jy}: at l=0 it is Warnaar's Con_JTBC (Eq_PCn), whose RHS sum_{la even, la_1<=2k} P_la(x;t) was computed from Macdonald's Hall-Littlewood symmetrisation formula -- a disjoint engine -- and agrees exactly at (n,k)=(3,1),(4,1),(3,2). Five of six exponent perturbations fail the gate; the row-vs-column placement of the linear term is a VACUOUS arm (passes at k=1,2) and is recorded as such.

A_alpha, B_alpha, TOT_alpha computed twice: from the cylindric Jacobi-Trudi determinant (HKKO eq CJT) and from HKKO's lattice-path model (walks in the affine alcove x_1>=..>=x_m>=x_1-w). Agree on all 476 contents compared at (k,w,n)=(1,2,4),(1,4,5),(2,2,4).

Lemma 2: a monomial weight only redistributes objects among powers of t, so sum_e max([t^e]c_alpha,0) <= A_alpha under HKKO's signs (S), and ||c_alpha||_1 <= TOT_alpha under arbitrary signs (S-plus-minus).

THEOREM (uniform in l). For every l>=0 set M=l+2, k=1, w=2M-2, n=N=2M, alpha=(1^n). Then c_alpha(t) = C_M - (2M-1)t^{M-1} + t^{M+1} with A_alpha=C_M (Dyck paths, ceiling inactive) and B_alpha=2M-2 (one down-step, admissible positions 2..2M-1). Since 2M-1 > 2M-2, (S) fails at every l: HKKO Thm 3.3 with t^{stat(T)} inserted is false for EVERY statistic. At l=0 (M=2) also TOT=A+B=4 < 6 = ||2-3t+t^3||_1, so even re-choosing the signs fails.

CORROBORATION, not a dependency -- the proof of the parent is complete by hand (Steps 1-4 of Thm 1 in the .tex), so this node is an attempt/check and not a premise. Witness formula and counts verified by exact symbolic computation at l=0,1,2 (c = 2-3t+t^3, 5-5t^2+t^4, 14-7t^3+t^5; A=2,5,14=C_M; B=2,4,6=2M-2) and at l=3 from the sweep (42-9t^4+t^6, A=42, B=8). Exhaustive per-monomial sweep over 15 parameter points, 59k monomials, with c_alpha(1)=A_alpha-B_alpha asserted on every one.
At (k,l,n)=(2,0,4), alpha=(2,2,2,2): c_alpha = 10-16t+11t^2-4t^3, ||.||_1 = 41 against TOT = 11. (S-plus-minus) fails by 30; 145 of 313 monomials violate it.

COROLLARY, and the session's actual answer: any Tr(D T^N) whose configurations are the cylindric tableaux with Boltzmann weight x^T and whose twist contributes a scalar per winding sector has the form sum_T eps(T) t^{stat(T)} x^T, hence is governed by the capacity lemma and cannot equal Eq_generalise at (k,l,n)=(1,0,4). The twist ansatz dies on CARDINALITY, not on the twist being diagonal and not on linear-vs-quadratic: a twist supplies one monomial per configuration and the target needs more.

Secondary and CONDITIONAL: a diagonal twist's exponent is additive in the sector label, whereas Warnaar's Q(y)=M sum y_i^2 - sum j y_i has Q(2e_1)-2Q(e_1)=2M != 0. So IF y is the winding sector then no diagonal twist reproduces it; the quadratic form is a level-M theta weight, i.e. an energy grading t^{L_0}, not a flavour twist t^{J_0}. The identification of y with the winding sector is NOT proved here, and the corollary above does not need it.

What survives as the answer: uniformly in l the deformation must attach a Laurent POLYNOMIAL pi_T(t) to each cylindric tableau, not a power of t. This is the shape of Macdonald III (5.8'),(5.9'),(5.11') pp.229-230: P_{la/mu} = sum_T psi_T(t) x^T with psi_T a product of factors (1 - t^{m_j(mu)}). At l=0 Warnaar's determinant IS a sum of Hall-Littlewood polynomials, so t is a bulk parameter (deforms a tableau count by products of 1-t^m) and not a boundary fugacity (which would deform it by a power). The quadratic Gaussian is what such a bulk weight SUMS TO after the affine folding, not what it IS on the tableau side. [UPDATED 2026-10-10 c2 PROVE: the named candidate -- 'exactly the shape of Macdonald's psi_T' -- is now REFUTED. Korff's cylindric psi exists and does not work, and nothing cyclically psi-graded does: see q410-no-cyclic-psi-weight. The surviving type is narrowed to weights with ord_{t=1} = 0 on some tableau of each fibre: see surviving-type-narrowed.]

The slack comes entirely from the shapes la in Par(2k,w) with c^-_{2k,w}(la)=0, invisible to HKKO Thm 3.3 -- at (1,1,6) the shape (4,2) supplies 9 of the 18 tableaux. Failing to violate a necessary condition is an absence of evidence, not evidence. Constructing pi_T(t), or a monomial statistic on the enlarged set for l>=1, is the real form of Warnaar's question.

children.approach: Dictionary (Prop 1 of the Q410 paper), proved two independent ways: Korff's n_K = h = 2k cyclic slots and k_K = w = 2ell+2 level. (i) shape parameters, via HKKO Prop 2.4 (CRST(la;h,w) <-> CSSYT(Tr(la;h,w);w,h), so the semistandard period is (w,-h)); (ii) state count, x in {x_1>=..>=x_h>=x_1-w} |-> m_i = x_i-x_{i+1}, m_h = w-(x_1-x_h), sum m_i = w on h cyclic sites, with m_i(x+theta)-m_i(x) = theta_i - theta_{i+1} which is verbatim Korff's own relation in his proof of Lemma 5.4. Korff's column index is the HKKO row index.

Korff (5.13) transported to HKKO lattice paths and implemented (code-1010-q410/korff.py). TWO GATES, EACH WITH CONTROLS THAT FIRE. Gate 1, Korff's printed eq (5.16) b_la*Psi = b_mu*Phi: true reading 0/180 violations; four deliberately wrong readings (non-cyclic index set; m_{i+1} for m_i; outer for inner multiplicities; I-set with m(mu)) violate 36, 88, 114, 88 of 180. Gate 2, non-cylindric reduction: true reading departs from Macdonald's psi only at order 6 and 7 at w=8,9 (the wrap factor's tail); every wrong reading departs at order 0. The cyclicity of the index set is therefore pinned by Korff's own lemma, not by my guess.

RECORDED VACUOUS, not a result. My first gate was 'Korff's P_{la/d/mu} is a symmetric function, so a wrong index set breaks symmetry'. Measured: symmetric for all 127 cylindric shapes tested at seven (h,w,nvars) -- AND symmetric for every wrong variant too, including the non-cyclic index set and Phi. The test is a constant function of the question and reports nothing. Replaced by the two gates above. Fourth entry on the 'a pass count does not report the rank of the test' axis.

Lemma: for theta in {0,1}^h, Korff's index set J(theta) = {i in Z/hZ : theta_i=0, theta_{i+1}=1} is empty iff theta is constant. Hence ord_{t=1} Psi_T = nu(T) := sum_a |J(theta^(a))| >= #{non-constant strips}; and at alpha=(1^n) with h>=2 every strip has exactly one box, is non-constant, and has |J|=1, so nu(T) = n for EVERY T. The region condition forces m_i >= 1 for i in J, so every factor is a genuine (1-t^m), m>=1, and Psi_T(0)=1.

MAIN RESULT OF Q410, and the answer is NO. Theorem: if (x..)^k * Eq_generalise = sum_T pi_T(t) x^T with pi cyclically psi-graded (ord_{t=1} pi_T >= nu(T)), then ord_{t=1} c_alpha >= min nu(T) over the fibre. Korff's Psi_T times ANY monomial t^{stat(T)} and ANY signs is cyclically psi-graded. Corollary at k=1, every ell>=0, n=N=2M, alpha=(1^n): nu(T)=2M for every T, while c_alpha = C_M-(2M-1)t^{M-1}+t^{M+1} has ord_{t=1} = 2 at M=2 (it is (1-t)^2(t+2)) and 0 for every M>=3 (since C_M > 2M-2 for M>=3, by C_3=5>4 and C_{M+1}/C_M = 2(2M+1)/(M+2) >= 2). So 2 < 4 <= 2M and the identity fails uniformly in ell. A monomial statistic cannot help because it is a unit at t=1 -- which is exactly why this is the right invariant.

Exact-arithmetic verification. (a) nu(T) takes the single value {n} over all T at alpha=(1^n) at six (k,ell,n). (b) Brute-force evaluation of Psi_T at t=1 on every tableau, compared against the cyclic-ascent prediction, agrees in 23891 of 23891 contents at seven (k,ell,n). (c) Ground truth c_alpha re-derived from the Warnaar determinant engine, independent of the Korff side, matching Q405's closed form at (1,0,4) and (1,1,6). (d) Violation table: 0, 0, 90, 301, 3025, 65, 7749 contents violating the t=1 identity at (1,0,3),(1,0,4),(1,1,5),(1,1,6),(1,2,8),(2,0,4),(2,1,6) -- the two ell=0 rows are ZERO and that is a fact about ell=0, not a failure of method (at h=w=2 the walk forces A_alpha=B_alpha whenever some alpha_a=1). (e) Two rows at k>=2 are VACUOUS: c_alpha == 0 at (2,0,5) and (2,1,7), so the theorem says nothing there; honest count four informative of six.

The failure is one integer. At ell=0, k=1, alpha=(1^4) the target IS a psi-weighted tableau sum -- over the two ORDINARY semistandard tableaux of shape (2,2), with Macdonald weights (1-t)^2 and (1-t)^2(1+t), each vanishing at exactly 2 of its 4 horizontal strips, summing to (1-t)^2(t+2) = 2-3t+t^3 = c_alpha. The four (2,2)-CYLINDRIC tableaux of the same content all carry the same Korff weight (1-t)^2(1-t^2)^2, vanishing at ALL 4 strips. Passing from Macdonald's open ascent set to Korff's cyclic one adds the wrap index i=h, which for a one-box strip in a 2-row cylinder fires exactly when the open one does not. Order 2 against order 4; and c_alpha/Psi = (t+2)/((1-t)^2(1+t)^2) is not a Laurent polynomial, so no statistic repairs it.

Psi_T(0) = 1 for every T, so Korff's P_{la/d/mu}(x;0) is the UNWEIGHTED cylindric Schur function; whereas HKKO's theorem says it is at t=1 that Warnaar's determinant becomes the unweighted cylindric count. Verified exactly: sum_T c^-(la(T)) Psi_T(0) = A_alpha - B_alpha = c_alpha(1) at (1,0,4) and (1,1,6) (0=0 and 1=1). The two deformations of the same object are normalised at opposite values of t. This is the one-sentence reason the identification cannot work, and it is why no reparametrisation t -> 1/t or monomial regrading saves it: ord_{t=1} is invariant under both.

NECESSARY CONDITION, proved: any weight pi solving Warnaar Sect 6 must have, at k=1, alpha=(1^{2M}), some T in the fibre with ord_{t=1} pi_T <= 2 (M=2) and = 0 (M>=3). So for M>=3 at least one cylindric tableau carries a weight that does NOT vanish at t=1 and hence is not a product of factors (1-t^m), m>=1, at all. This rules out psi_T, phi_T, Korff's Psi_T and Phi_T, and every monomial regrading of them.

SPECULATIVE, the pointer not the theorem: the surviving type should be a ratio with as many (1-t^a) factors above as below -- a Gaussian-binomial type, whose t=1 value is the ordinary binomial, so that the t=1 specialisation returns HKKO's unweighted count. That points at the modified Hall-Littlewood / Kostka-Foulkes normalisation rather than at branching coefficients. Not tested.

RECORDED, NOT USED. Two of Korff's standing restrictions already exclude the target under the dictionary. (i) He assumes n_K > 2 throughout, i.e. 2k > 2, i.e. k >= 2; the witness family has k=1 and sits at n_K = 2. (ii) His Def 5.5 defines P_{la/d/mu}(x_1..x_{ell_K};t) for 1 <= ell_K <= k_K and SETS IT TO ZERO for ell_K > k_K; here ell_K = n (number of variables) and k_K = w, and the witness has n = N = 2k+w > w, so his own convention makes the function vanish identically wherever Warnaar's question has content. I dropped the convention and tested the FORMULA, because answering a mathematical question by a convention is not an answer; the combinatorics is visibly non-empty there (4 cylindric tableaux of content (1^4) at h=w=2).

DEAD END as a gate. Korff's Example 5.1 (n_K=5, k_K=6, three strips) lists index sets {3,6},{4},{4,6} -- five elements -- and prints the weight as (1-t)^4(1-t^2)^2, which is SIX factors; and the listed sets contain 6 > n_K = 5, which the stated index range 1 <= i <= n_K excludes. I wanted it as the independent printed-display gate (the move that built star.py from two printed displays) and could not decode it.

Q416 (THE WRAP-FACTOR CONJECTURE, opened by BROWSE 2026-10-10 c3 hours before this session) RESOLVED: first half TRUE, conclusion REFUTED. Proved: under the dictionary, Korff's Psi(x,theta) = Macdonald's psi(x,theta) times exactly one wrap factor (1-t^{w-(x_1-x_h)}), active iff theta_h=0 and theta_1=1, i.e. iff the strip wraps -- that is Q416's architecture 'cylindric = finite object + ONE wrap-around correction', and it is a theorem (checked on 934/934 strips at seven (h,w), with the no-wrap control disagreeing on 27). REFUTED: Q416's conclusion that 'the polynomial weight Q410 wants is the finite weight times a wrap factor, NOT a new statistic'. By the cyclic-ascent lemma the wrap is active at EVERY strip of EVERY tableau of content (1^n), so at ell=0 all four tableaux have fold count 4, not 2, and all carry the same (1-t)^2(1-t^2)^2. The wrap factor pushes ord_{t=1} in the WRONG direction: from the 2 that Macdonald's psi supplies on the two ordinary SSYT of shape (2,2) up to 4. PRIORITY, recorded honestly: the ell=0 form of this invariant -- 'ord_{t=1}(2-3t+t^3) = exactly 2, so every one of the four tableaux needs >= 2 folds and one exactly 2' -- was found FIRST, by BROWSE 10-10 c3 the same morning, together with the Ram/Schwer identification of the psi/phi weight as (1-t)^{#folds}. What is new here is the dictionary, the cyclic-ascent lemma that makes the fold count n uniformly, the measurement that Korff's count is n and not 2, and the uniform-in-ell theorem.
